bottleneck: Mechanics around the task: although the image installs RDKit, the default python3 is the verifier virtual environment and cannot import it. All 12 scored attempts first spent turns trying unavailable pip commands, conflicting package installs, or alternate interpreters before doing the chemistry; the two strongest reconstructed submissions then failed only canonical tautomer standardization.
change: Repair the broken setup in the environment by putting /usr/bin before the verifier virtual environment on PATH, so the ordinary python3 command reaches the image-installed RDKit. This is structural help around the retained skill and removes package/interpreter troubleshooting; it does not supply any molecular correction, standardization decision, descriptor, filter result, or output row. The original signal the student can now reach directly is RDKit's parse and standardization behavior on library.tsv.
restore: A later harder version can remove the PATH override, returning interpreter discovery and package setup to the student without changing the chemistry task.
prediction: The change addresses the repeated first action of attempting to install or locate RDKit after python3 cannot import it. With python3 able to import RDKit immediately, students can next inspect parse failures and test canonical tautomerization instead of spending early turns on pip and interpreter conflicts. This prediction is refuted if the next 12 attempts still spend their opening work on making RDKit importable, or if none reach molecular standardization sooner.
